content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.
When this app is finished, what should be different for you compared with how you handle bookmarks today?

Honestly, today my bookmarks are a mess — they live in different browsers, the names are whatever the page happened to be called, and I can never find anything later. So when this is done, here's what I'd want to feel different.

When I save a link, I just want to paste the address and have it sort itself out — pull in the page's title, a short description, the little site icon, maybe a picture — so I'm not typing all that by hand. And if I ever try to save something I already saved, I don't want a second copy; I'd want it to just take me to the one I already have so I can tweak it.

Then, finding things again should be the easy part. I want to search across everything — the titles, my own notes, the descriptions, the web address — without worrying about capital letters. I want to label things with my own tags and click a tag to see just those. And I'd love to stash things as "read this later" and be able to pull up just that pile when I have time, then check them off as I get through them.

I also want to keep the stuff I care about from disappearing on me — so if a page goes away later, I still have what it said saved somewhere.

That's the heart of it for me. What are you picturing so far?

content:
I’m picturing a personal bookmark home base that:

- Makes saving nearly effortless by filling in the page details automatically.
- Prevents duplicate copies and brings you back to the existing bookmark.
- Lets you reliably rediscover links through broad, case-insensitive search and your own tags.
- Gives you a focused “read later” pile you can work through and check off.
- Preserves the page’s contents so important material remains available even if the original disappears.

The real goal seems to be turning scattered, forgettable links into an organized, searchable personal library you can trust. Is that the direction you mean?

Yes, that's exactly the direction — turning a pile of scattered, forgettable links into a library I actually trust and can find my way around.

A couple of things I'd add to make sure we're on the same page, since you captured the spirit well:

When I said tags, I don't just mean sticking labels on — I want it to help me while I type, suggesting tags I've already used so I don't end up with "recipe" and "recipes" and "cooking" all meaning the same thing. And searching should feel smart: I want to be able to search by a tag specifically, and combine things — like "show me anything about Rome that's either an article or a book" — not just type one word and hope.

On the reading side, "read later" is one thing, but I also picture the list itself being pleasant to skim — I should see the title, the description, and the tags right there, and clicking an item should just take me to the actual page.

And the whole thing is just for me — my own personal home base. I'm not thinking about other people logging in or sharing.
